newsitem.title: UK: GKN shares open higher, cheered by appeal.
newsitem.headline: GKN shares open higher, cheered by appeal.

text.p: Shares in engineering group GKN Plc bounced on Friday, opening sharply higher, after the company said it planned to appeal against a U.S. court decision to award the company record damages of $601 million. The shares recovered to be up 22p to 996p by 0833 GMT, after earlier dipping to 950p in pre-market trade. GKN said it will appeal the U.S. district court ruling against its Meineke Discount Muffler division, as soon as possible. A jury found that Meineke had misused advertising fees and defrauded its franchisees.
"The damages were higher than anticipated but they are going to fight it," said one senior trader. "It doesn't automatically follow that they were have to pay out that much."
GKN said last month that it expected the award to be about 30 percent lower than the $740 million originally feared. The company has cash reserves of around $850 million.

"The shares fell out of bed last night when we got the news in the States and now people are turning to the dividend and wondering if it's in danger and whether dividend growth is safe," said one trader.
"The answer we're getting is yes, because of their net cash position. So the argument is that on a big weakness like this the shares should then be bought, and that is what we're seeing."
